subject: Renewal: capacity banding and proposed premium support add-on
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: 2028-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal window coming up — capacity needs + SLA questions

Evelyn,

Hope you’re well. We’re kicking off renewal planning for our platform contract (current term ends 2028-12-31) and I wanted to loop you in on two priority asks from our infra and procurement teams:

1) Capacity banding — peak concurrency has grown 3x year-over-year. We expect a baseline reserved capacity increase to cover 9k concurrent tokens with burst up to 18k for campaign windows. We’d like to understand how Redwood would price a capacity band (base + burst). I’ve attached a short workbook with our usage patterns.

2) Premium SLA — we’ve been evaluating options for a faster latency SLO (p99) and a tighter incident response matrix (24/7 phone escalation + 15-minute P1 callback). Is that something Redwood offers as an add-on at renewal? If so, what are the lead times and contract commitments?

Can we schedule 30 minutes next week to go over this? I can include our procurement lead if useful.

Thanks,
Liam
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

Attachments: MAA-ACME-2028-capacity.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window coming up — capacity needs + SLA questions

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the workbook, that’s helpful context. Happy to run through options. Quick answers up front:

- Capacity banding: yes — we can set a committed baseline with a defined burst band. We typically model price in three bands (baseline, burst1, burst2) with clear overage rates.
- Premium SLA: Redwood offers an add-on with 24/7 phone escalation and a P1 initial response commitment (15 min) for enterprise customers on a reserved capacity commit. We’ll need a firm baseline commit (12 months minimum) for the short SLO and phone coverage.

I’ve attached a draft Premium SLA amendment and a one-pager on our capacity banding constructs. Can we do Tue 10/17 9:30am PT? I’ll bring Marissa (solutions) and loop in Rishi for pricing.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Premium_SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf (draft), Capacity_Banding_OnePager.pdf
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal window coming up — capacity needs + SLA questions

Team — forwarding Liam's note and the workbook. Key asks: baseline ~9k concurrents, burst to 18k, P1 15m, 24/7 phone.

My thinking: propose a two-tier band with a 12-month baseline commit and a reserved burst band that can be purchased as seasonal capacity (3 month min). For pricing, we should offer two commercial paths:

- 1-year term, baseline commit at current growth-adjusted rate + 18% uplift for Premium SLA (phone + 15m P1).
- 2-year term, baseline commit with annual true-up, price uplift capped at 12% year 1 and 8% year 2, include 10% discount on burst band.

Rishi — can you run a quick calc (cost per token/hour and per-concurrency) using the attached workbook and target an internal markup that keeps gross margin at target? Priyom — any dependency on legal for the SLA language (escalation matrix, credits) I should flag now?

Would like to present these options at meeting on 10/17.

— Evelyn
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@acme-corp.com>, acme-procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: 2028-11-01T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window coming up — capacity needs + SLA questions

Evelyn,

Thanks for the options — we reviewed internally. A few follow-ups from infra/procurement:

- The two-year path looks interesting because it gives us predictability. Can you confirm whether the 15-minute P1 is an SLA-backed creditable metric (ie, do we get financial credits if missed)?
- For phone escalation, we need a named escalation contact list and a runbook handoff. Can Redwood support a partnership onboarding call with our SREs for runbook alignment?
- Procurement asked about billing cadence — they prefer annual billing with a purchase order at renewal and a single PO for both baseline + expected burst commitment.

I’m copying Dana (procurement) to start the PO conversation. If you can send a revised amendment with the two-year commercial path and DocuSign link, we’ll review legally.

— Liam

Attachments: none
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>, Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-14T10:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window coming up — capacity needs + SLA questions

Hi Liam & Dana —

Appreciate the clarity. Answers/next steps below:

- SLA credits: yes — the Premium SLA amendment includes a measurable P1 response time (15 min) and financial credits for missed response or missed p99 latency targets. Language is in section 4 of the attached amendment.
- Escalation/runbook: we’ll schedule a 60-minute runbook alignment workshop between our on-call SRE and Acme SREs. Marissa will coordinate dates and own the runbook template.
- Billing: annual billing with a single PO is fine; we’ll reflect that in the commercial terms.

Attached: revised Redwood_Premium_SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf with the two-year pricing appendix and DocuSign package link (inline). Dana — when you have the procurement PO number we’ll route countersignature through DocuSign.

DocuSign: https://docusign.net/abcdef

Next steps: 1) Dana to draft PO, 2) runbook alignment call (Marissa to propose 3 slots), 3) countersign in DocuSign.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
